summary: Modular monolith: NestJS + Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL serving SvelteKit, hosted on Google Cloud Run (us-central1 Iowa). Estimated $450-1,700/month (around the $600 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: One deployable with strict internal modules for the ecommerce domain: a 3-engineer team gets clear boundaries without distributed-system overhead; modules can be extracted later if scale demands it. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 3 engineer(s), no DevOps cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Web - SvelteKit: Chosen because team already works in javascript (team.languages); server-rendered/pre-rendered HTML for seo_critical=true; strong performance (5/5) with priorities.performance=3; rich client-side interactivity for a ecommerce.

alternatives.why_not: SvelteKit scores higher on performance and learning curve (fit 7.6 vs 8.1).
SvelteKit scores higher on performance (fit 7.5 vs 8.1).

tradeoffs: Smaller ecosystem and talent pool than React/Vue

backend.justification: Chosen because team already works in javascript (team.languages); strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; modules/DI give structure for a ecommerce domain; same language as the web/mobile clients: shared types and validation code.

alternatives.why_not: Complex ecommerce workflows outgrow BaaS rules and edge functions; high vendor lock-in (proprietary APIs/data model) with lock-in tolerance 'medium'. NestJS scores higher on maintainability (fit 6.8 vs 7.3).
NestJS scores higher on platform coverage and scalability (fit 6.7 vs 7.3).

tradeoffs: Single-threaded event loop: CPU-heavy work must go to workers

database.choice: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL (us-central1 Iowa, HA standby)
database.justification: Chosen because relational integrity and transactions for a ecommerce domain; strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=3. Managed as Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL: same platform and private network as the application hosting; fully managed: no operations work for a team without DevOps.

alternatives.why_not: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 5.5 vs 6.2).
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 5.1 vs 6.2).
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL scores higher on integration with the hosting platform (fit -0.4 vs 1.7).
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=managed_cloud: self-managed VMs/databases are excluded in favour of managed services.

tradeoffs: Single-writer primary: write scale beyond one large node needs partitioning/sharding
Vacuum and connection pooling need attention at scale
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL starts around $240/month against a $600/month total budget

hosting.justification: Chosen because strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=3; strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; runs the NestJS (Node.js LTS, TypeScript) container as-is.

tradeoffs: WebSocket connections capped by request timeout (max 60 min): clients must reconnect
